method: web tool; primary sources only; no human interviews; scopes per record

sources.title: ADHD in Adults: 4 Things to Know
sources.supports: Difficulties and individual variation are legitimate design context, not product efficacy.

sources.title: NIMH Expert Dr Mary Rooney Discusses Managing ADHD
sources.supports: Initiating and sustaining a task can differ across individuals.
sources.limits: Not evidence for any optimal UI or timer.

sources.title: Give me a break! A systematic review and meta-analysis on the efficacy of micro-breaks for increasing well-being and performance
sources.design: 19 records; 22 independent samples; N=2335; healthy employees/students; breaks up to 10 min.
sources.supports: Small vigor and fatigue benefits; overall performance effect not significant.
sources.limits: Not ADHD specific; no universal optimal duration; activity subtypes inadequately resolved.

sources.title: The Effects of Gamification on Computerized Cognitive Training: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.supports: Motivation/engagement and demand both increase; no corresponding training-domain benefit established.
sources.limits: Cognitive training is not microrest; mixed populations and limited studies.

sources.title: Tasks Interrupted: How Anticipating Time Pressure on Resumption of an Interrupted Task Causes Attention Residue and Low Performance on Interrupting Tasks and How a Ready-to-Resume Plan Mitigates the Effects
sources.supports: Planning resumption may mitigate attention residue in the studied situation.
sources.limits: Outcome includes interrupting task performance; not an ADHD extension trial.

sources.title: Directing smartphone use through the self-nudge app one sec
sources.read: PMC full-text extract returned by web search; direct open returned browser check, not bypassed.
sources.design: N=280 six-week continuing field users; N=500 randomized online experiment.
sources.supports: A simple option to dismiss consumption deserves comparison with combined interventions.
sources.limits: Field selection/attrition, online video setting, no ADHD-specific efficacy; one author originated app.

sources.title: I Just Want to Hack Myself to Not Get Distracted: Evaluating Design Interventions for Self-Control on Facebook
sources.design: 58 students; three interventions over six weeks.
sources.supports: Goal reminders and removed feed may help control, with annoyance/FOMO tradeoffs.
sources.limits: Not validation of dh-focus current implementation; not ADHD specific.

sources.title: Not Just Me and My To-Do List: Understanding Challenges of Task Management for Adults with ADHD and the Need for AI-Augmented Social Scaffolds
sources.read: author manuscript abstract and version metadata
sources.design: 22 interviews plus 20 different participants reviewing 13 speculative concepts.
sources.supports: Task management may require emotional and social scaffolding.
sources.limits: ADHD-identifying participants; qualitative concepts not outcome trial; author-reported CSCW acceptance, publication not independently verified.

sources.title: Effects of interventions to reduce the negative consequences of interruptions on task performance: A systematic review, meta-analysis, and narrative synthesis of laboratory studies
sources.supports: Interruption interventions vary by task and intervention.
sources.limits: Laboratory and abstract-only evidence, not field or ADHD-specific product validation.
